title: CoolSynth Listening Pass
intro: Only what needs your ears, each with something to judge it against: ▶ Play against a try (a before and after), or a plain question with a few answers. What you passed on the 19th and 20th is left out (Chip, Arcade, the SVF, the stutter drafts, three noise presets). The kicks are mine first, measured against the real 808 and 909 recordings; the DAW checks are mine too.

groups.title: The TB-303
groups.intro: Built on the 20th from Open303's engine (D242). Fixed today: Acid had a hidden Ladder filter after the 303 (its bank entry named no P1); it now plays the 303 alone, levelled again. Notes at velocity 100 or more are accented; overlapping notes slide.

groups.title: The Ladder by ear
groups.intro: Item 13: four questions the measurements can't settle. Basic Saw through the Ladder at 800 Hz, nothing else moving it.

groups.title: The added hiss and crackle
groups.intro: Item 18: the presets with tape hiss or record crackle you haven't judged yet (Vinyl Choir, Concrete Pad and Pirate Radio passed on the 20th), each against itself with both at zero. Built on the 19th (D221): a steady level that mutes in silence.

groups.title: Chip: the card left from the 20th
groups.intro: You passed the rest of Chip, Arcade and the SVF on the 20th. This one was left unmarked.

groups.title: Workshop
groups.intro: Workshop: starting points. One generator, the filter wide open, short envelopes, no effects. Basic Noise (noise generator, phase 3.1), Basic FM (FM generator, 3.2) and Basic Wavetable (3.4) follow.

groups.title: Bedroom
groups.intro: Bedroom: lo-fi and cozy. Soft attacks, warm tops, a little air, worn tape and dusty vinyl.

groups.title: Arcade
groups.intro: Arcade: chip sounds. Pulse waves at 12.5, 25 and 50 percent, arpeggio-fast pitch, periodic noise. Thin, fast, cheerful. Room rule: filter open, no reverb, at most one slap of delay. Revoiced with the Chip generator on 2026-11-20 (D231), drafts for the user's ears; the VA versions are in git.

groups.title: Outrun
groups.intro: Outrun: synthwave. Stacked saws, chorus, synced delay and reverb on everything, gated rhythms, bright and wide. Produced, where Studio 1982 is played.

groups.title: Observatory
groups.intro: Observatory: space and ambient. Slow swells, wide stereo, long tails, no hurry.

groups.title: Greenhouse
groups.intro: Greenhouse: glass, bells, mallets and strings. Percussive attacks, inharmonic or sine-rich decays, organic. Room rule: sustain level 0 everywhere.

groups.title: Basement
groups.intro: Basement: dark industrial and techno. Distortion and resonance, low, menacing, metallic; sweeps that scream. Nothing pretty. Room rule: drive or fold on every preset.

groups.title: Studio 1982
groups.intro: Studio 1982: clean polysynth classics with audible filter envelopes and light effects. Played, not produced: at most one or two effects per preset.

groups.title: Main Stage
groups.intro: Main Stage: modern, wide, processed. Most of this room waits for later modules.

groups.title: Engine Room
groups.intro: Engine Room: one of each bass family, mono or legato, tight, no reverb.

groups.title: Clock Tower
groups.intro: Clock Tower: motion. The rhythm comes from the patch itself (arps, Euclid, ratchets, the step modulator, synced LFOs). Every preset is tempo-locked; hold one note or a chord.

groups.title: Conservatory
groups.intro: Conservatory: the sampled instruments, one plain preset each. The room is divided into families; an instrument's ways of being played are the Sample generator's Style inside its preset. Written by tools/audition/make_conservatory.py from resources/instruments/catalogue.txt.

groups.title: Museum
groups.intro: Museum: classic synth sounds rebuilt from their published settings, each converted to this engine's units and admitted by the user in a side-by-side against a reference recording (decisions D88, D103, D104, D107). No effects: the sounds are as the instrument made them. Candidates wait in resources/museum-candidates, outside the plugin.

groups.title: Night Bus
groups.intro: Night Bus: the ride between the club and the bedroom, headphones on (D206). Laptop music made out of pieces of other things: a voice turned into texture, everything a little worn, warm underneath. After Caribou, Loukeman, Vegyn, ear and meat computer (docs/research/sound-references.md). Room rule: the Pitch effect is in every preset (a shadow an octave away, a wide doubling, a staircase of echoes): its warble is this room's glue, where the Bedroom's is tape.

items.title: Acid: a 303 line

items.title: Accent: with against without
listen: ▶ Play has accents on six of the sixteen steps; the try plays every step at the same velocity.

items.title: Slide: with against without

listen: The idea: "Emerson's Fat Bass from Brain Salad Surgery", from Tom Rhea's Sound Charts for the Minimoog (Moog Music, 1974, page 15). The chart: three sawtooth oscillators at full level, one at 32' and two at 16', tuned to unison; filter cutoff -2, emphasis 5, amount of contour 3.5, both keyboard-control switches on; filter contour attack 0, decay 300 msec, sustain 0; loudness contour attack 0, decay 600 msec, sustain 5; decay switch on, no glide. One voice; a note joined to the one before it does not start the filter's sweep again, a note struck anew does, and that sweep at every struck note is the sound. The chart also has the filter-modulation switch on with the wheel a little raised: oscillator 3 shakes the cutoff at its own pitch, a growl more than a wobble. items.title: TX81Z LatelyBass
listen: The idea: The Yamaha TX81Z's LatelyBass (1987, preset C15): the bass of late-eighties house and new jack swing. Play it around the octave under middle C: it sounds two octaves under the key, as on the instrument (the voice is transposed an octave down and its carrier runs at half the note). The voice, from the instrument's own preset table (read out of its firmware): algorithm 2, two modulators into one into the carrier. The carrier and the modulator on it run at the same pitch (1.7 radians at a hard key, fading with the note): the round, hollow body. On that modulator sit two more an octave higher, both gone within a third of a second: a sine with full feedback (3 radians at a hard key: the bark), and one on the TX81Z's fifth wave, a whole sine squeezed into half the cycle (1.3 radians: the click). A light key leaves most of the bark out; the note itself is as loud at any velocity, as on the instrument. A slow wobble of pitch, five cents either way, is the voice's own LFO. Nothing is fitted: levels, ratios, rates, rate scaling and the velocity law (the firmware's table) are the chip's rules converted; the feedback follows operator 4's level, as on the chip. Against a recording of a real TX81Z playing this voice (one note, hardest velocity) the first sixteen harmonics are within 0.9 dB on average over half a second, and against the chip's rules within 0.3 to 1.4 dB over fifteen keys and velocities.
